To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the performance of an active learning system is dependent on the type of classifier and on the selection strategy.

active learning strategies can be used to improve the efficiency of the labeling process for prosodic annotation tasks, and that these strategies can be successfully applied to the annotation of prosodic boundaries as well as pitch accents.
the active selection of training data is a viable alternative to random selection and that it is possible to achieve a good performance with as little as 50% of the labeled data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
exploring the use of active learning strategies to reduce the amount of human annotation required in the training of prosody models.
exploring and evaluating the effectiveness of active learning techniques to reduce the amount of human-labeled data needed to train a prosodic-event classifier.

the development of active-learning strategies to guide the selection and labeling of data for the annotation of prosodic events, and the evaluation of these strategies for the annotation of pitch accents and prosody boundaries in English.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in most of the cases, active learning is an effective strategy for reducing the amount of data needed to attain the desired performance level.
active learning can be used to reduce by a factor of 2 the number of data points required to achieve the same performance as random selection.
, for the case of the annotation of pitch accents and prosody breaks, active learning is a very effective strategy to reduce the amount of human annotation required to train a classifier.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
active-learning methods are a good alternative to reduce the amount of data needed to train a prosodic event classifier.
the performance of the active-learning methods is very similar to random selection for pitch accent and boundary labeling.

active learning strategies for selecting data to label are effective for prosodic event labeling and can be used to significantly reduce the amount of data needed to achieve a given level of accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for this specific task, the use of active learning strategies does not necessarily require the use of complex selection criteria and can lead to substantial reductions in the amount of labeled data needed for training a classifier.
the use of active learning strategies is a promising direction for reducing the cost of human annotation in tasks that require large amounts of labeled data.
, in general, active learning techniques can be successfully applied for the task of prosodic annotation.
